title: Standup snapshot: kernel shim + KV safety
body:
Summary
-----
Quick capture from today's kernel/kv-batching sync (2026-03-23). Focus: landing the kernel shim that isolates kernel patch side-effects, validating KV cache safety under split-batch conditions, and a lightweight experiment to reduce batch jitter for sub-2s tails. This is a working snapshot — open questions flagged below.

Attendees
---------
Priya Nair (owner), Ethan Park, Sofia Alvarez, Benji Li, Margo Chen (observability), oncall: Dan O.

High-level takeaways
--------------------
- Kernel shim PR (#812) is functionally green on unit tests but failing one integration test that surfaces under high-concurrency (JIRA-OPS-2891). Root cause appears to be a race in kernel handshake + prefill invalidation.
- KV cache safety checks show 98.7% hit-rate on long-running prefix hits in the shadow sampler, but a small class of stale-prefill reads caused 0.3% incorrect KV lookups under load.
- Micro-batch jitter experiment (cohort sampler v2) reduced p95 token latency by ~18% for small requests (sequences <64) in bench harness. Real traffic A/B (10% traffic) shows p95 improvement ~10% but p99 unchanged.

Metrics & quick numbers (latest 24h synthetic/bench)
--------------------------------------------------
- Kernel shim bench (synthetic concurrent 400 clients): p50 10ms, p95 120ms, p99 310ms (baseline p95 145ms).
- KV shadow sampler: hit-rate 98.7% (long prefix), miss amplification factor 1.11 (i.e., miss causes 11% more downstream compute), stale-prefill fraction 0.3% of reads in worst bucket.
- Micro-batch jitter experiment: tail variance down 28%, average tokens/sec per GPU up 6%.
- Incidents: one 5-minute elevated error-rate window yesterday caused by handshake race; oncall captured core dump (see linked artifact JIRA-OPS-2891).

What we tried this week
----------------------
1) Kernel shim (#812)
   - Purpose: introduce a minimal boundary layer so kernel-level retries and new handshake semantics don't leak scheduling invariants into higher layers.
   - Status: unit tests passing; integration fails intermittently under high concurrent warms. Reproduced locally with stress harness.
   - Observations: race between kernel handshake reply and KV prefill invalidation; when kernel replies before prefill mark completes the cache can be read with partially-applied KV pointers.

2) KV cache safety instrumenting
   - Added a verification micro-check that validates KV tag versions when reading from cache in shadow mode. Emits a new metric kv.read.version_mismatch.
   - Shadow run over 48h on staging shows version_mismatch spikes aligned with kernel handshake failures. Correlation is strong but causality still being debated.

3) Micro-batch jitter mitigation (cohort sampler v2)
   - Tuned sampler to prefer coalescing short requests with matching model shapes vs strict time-window waits.
   - Reduced artificial batching timeouts for sequences <64 from 8ms -> 4ms; added conservative backoff for GPU warmup sequences.

Open questions / hypotheses
---------------------------
- Is the handshake race caused by ordering of kernel-side ack vs prefill write? Hypothesis: our prefill mark is asynchronous and not barrier-synchronized with kernel handshake completion. Suggest: add a confirmation step in shim to guarantee prefill commit before exposing reply.
- Stale-prefill root cause: are we evicting during read due to concurrent compaction? We need deeper heap/eviction traces from the cache compactor.
- Micro-batch experiment: p99 didn't improve — suspect noise from cross-tenant heavy requests that sit outside sampler heuristics. Need to expand A/B to additional 25% traffic with heavier tenant mix.

Action items (owners + due dates)
---------------------------------
- Priya: Add shim-level prefill barrier in a small patch, submit PR and bench by Mon 2026-03-29. Linked to JIRA-OPS-2891.
- Ethan: Produce eviction trace export from cache compactor for the problematic bucket; due Thu 2026-03-26.
- Sofia: Run extended A/B for cohort sampler v2 on 25% traffic for 72h; collect p50/p95/p99 and per-tenant breakdown; due Tue 2026-03-30.
- Benji: Harden integration test harness to simulate kernel handshake reorderings; aim for flakiness <1% on CI; due Fri 2026-03-27.
- Margo: Add kv.read.version_mismatch to daily dashboard and alert threshold if >0.5% sustained for 10m; set up alert by Wed 2026-03-25.

Blockers & risks
----------------
- Kernel changes in the shim risk increasing latency if we add synchronous barriers. Must measure before widening rollout.
- Eviction traces are large; exporting them may require temporary higher S3 quota (ops ticket raised).
- Running extended A/B increases load on staging/VGPU pools; coordinate with infra to avoid interference with other experiments.

Notes from oncall (Dan O.)
-------------------------
- During the 5-min error window, the kernel returned CTX_NOT_READY for ~120 calls, downstream library retries exacerbated queue depth leading to transient saturation of a kernel worker. Patch workaround: increase per-kernel worker queue size by 2x to smooth retries (temporary).
- Oncall recommends we add a defensive early-return when kernel handshake throws CTX_NOT_READY so we avoid retry storms.

Design alternatives discussed briefly
-----------------------------------
- Option A: Sync prefill commit in shim (strong consistency, likely increase ~2-4ms tail).
- Option B: Keep async commit but add version-check and automatic fallback to re-prefill on mismatch (more complex but keeps latency low for the common case).
- Option C: Move prefill write into kernel commit flow (needs kernel-side work and broader rollout; higher engineering cost).

Decisions & next steps
----------------------
- Short-term: implement Option B variant (version-check + fallback) as quick mitigation while continuing to prototype Option A in parallel. Priya to own both experiments.
- Stabilize integration test harness (Benji) and schedule re-run of shim PR once Benji's harness is ready.

Misc notes / todo brain dump
---------------------------
- Look into compacting eviction windows to avoid compactor thrashing when cohort sampler changes request shapes.
- Add a lightweight sampled stack-trace when kv.read.version_mismatch increments to aid root-cause.
- Cross-ref with console team about exposing kv mismatch spikes to per-customer incident dashboard (SLA sensitive).

Next sync
---------
- Quick checkpoint Wed 2026-03-25 09:30 PT (15m) to confirm instrumentation and infra support. Full follow-up sync Mon 2026-03-29 11:00 PT (30m) to review shim bench and A/B progress.

Appendix: quick reproduction notes (engineers who want to repro locally)
-------------------------------------------------------------------
- Stress harness parameters: 400 concurrent clients, shape profile 'small-chat', prefill-size sampled 1.2x baseline, kernel handshake reorder injected with 1–3ms jitter. Repro steps in repo: ./dev/stress/run_kernel_reorder.sh --clients 400 --jitter 3ms.
- Integration test to look at: integration/test_kv_prefill_handshake.py (in PR #812).

End of snapshot.
